nfr_mechanisms: Partition/cluster-pruned BigQuery query filtering on customer_id and dtime_utc >= now-30d so the rolling-window lookup avoids full-table scans and meets the p95<500ms read budget.
Short-TTL (default 60s) in-process cache keyed by (country, operator, brand, customer_id) fronting the score computation to raise cache-hit rate above 80% and hold p99<1000ms under load.

country+operator+brand tenant predicate injected server-side from the authenticated caller's context into every measurement query — never client-supplied — so cross-tenant rows are structurally excluded.
customer_id validated at the API boundary with a typed/allow-list schema before any query executes; structured 400 on malformed input.
Response payload limited to score, status, and data_freshness_days (ADR-X002 data minimisation); customer_id is not echoed beyond the internal API boundary.
TLS 1.2+ termination and OWASP API Top 10 protections enforced at the Connectivity API Gateway; in-service API-key middleware as defense-in-depth.
Secrets (internal API key) stored in GCP Secret Manager and accessed via Workload Identity; none committed to the repo.
structlog JSON structured logging plus OpenTelemetry FastAPI tracing to Cloud Trace; connectivity metrics remain BigQuery-based per the service observability exception.

reviews.cost_notes: BigQuery scan cost is bounded by partition pruning to a single customer's 30-day slice; the short-TTL cache removes >80% of repeat queries. No new datastore is provisioned, so there is no incremental storage cost.
reviews.data_notes: Read-only aggregation over existing BigQuery fact tables; a mandatory country+operator+brand predicate on every query prevents cross-tenant combination. The service owns no authoritative in-life state, so C003 per-operator database ownership/isolation obligations are satisfied by not introducing a persistent store; if a store is later added it must follow C003.

reviews.privacy_notes: ADR-X002 data minimisation — the response carries only score, status, and data_freshness_days; operator-internal customer identifiers are not exposed to third parties and per-market data-residency is respected by querying within-jurisdiction data.

Trigger criteria: error rate >1% or sustained p95>500ms on the score route. No data migration to reverse (read-only). Rollback is validated in staging before production; owner is the connectivity backend on-call.

The workflow performs AUTOMATIC traffic rollback to the previous Cloud Run revision on any smoke-test failure at any promotion step (gcloud run services update-traffic --to-revisions <previous>=100) before any further promotion, with no manual intervention. doc.summary: Build a new internal-only read endpoint GET /api/v1/customers/{customer_id}/connectivity-score in the connectivity FastAPI service. A thin route delegates to a new scoring service module that reads a customer's last-30-days SamKnows measurements from the existing BigQuery fact tables (via the BigQueryAdapter), aggregates them across all associated devices, and returns a 0-100 weighted score (download 50%, upload 25%, latency 25%, each normalized to the customer's provisioned plan), a four-band status, and data_freshness_days (floor days since the most recent measurement of any type). The service owns no new persistent store — it is a stateless read model over already-ingested data. Tenant (country+operator+brand) filtering is injected server-side into every query; a short-TTL cache and partition-pruned queries hold the p95<500ms read SLO; internal-only access is enforced by an in-service API-key middleware behind the Connectivity API Gateway (OAuth/OIDC).

tasks.description: Add a Pydantic response model (src/connectivity/models/score.py) carrying only score:int, status:Literal[excellent,good,degraded,critical], and data_freshness_days:int — the ADR-X002 data-minimisation minimum. Validate the customer_id path parameter at the boundary with a typed/allow-list schema before any query; return a structured 400 on malformed input without leaking internal identifiers or SQL errors.
tasks.name: Add typed score request/response schema and customer_id boundary validation

tasks.description: Add src/connectivity/services/scoring.py with pure functions: per-metric sub-scores expressed relative to the customer's provisioned plan (throughput as measured/provisioned mbps capped at max, latency inverse), weighted average (download 0.5, upload 0.25, latency 0.25), status band derivation (>80 excellent; >60-80 good; >40-60 degraded; <=40 critical, ties to lower band), aggregation of all device measurements into one customer-level score, partial-metric handling (score from the metrics present when one of three is missing), and data_freshness_days = floor(days since the most recent measurement completion time of any test type across all devices; <24h -> 0; capped by the 30-day window).
tasks.name: Add scoring service module for sub-scores, weighted score, status band, and data_freshness_days

tasks.description: Add src/connectivity/services/measurements.py that builds and runs parameterized queries via the BigQueryAdapter against fact_httpget, fact_httppost, fact_udplatency (scored metrics) and fact_udpjitter (freshness only). Every query carries a mandatory WHERE predicate on country+operator+brand (from the authenticated caller's tenant context, validated server-side — never client-supplied) plus customer_id and dtime_utc >= now-30d, so no cross-tenant rows are ever returned. Filtered rows are returned to Python for aggregation; the mock adapter continues to return rows for credential-free tests.
tasks.name: Add tenant-scoped 30-day BigQuery measurement query across all SamKnows fact tables

tasks.description: Add src/connectivity/api/routes/score.py with GET /api/v1/customers/{customer_id}/connectivity-score: resolve tenant context, call the measurements query and scoring service, return HTTP 200 {score, status, data_freshness_days} when the customer has >=1 measurement of any type in the window, and HTTP 404 when the customer has no measurements of any type. Register the router in connectivity.main.create_app() alongside health and ingest.
tasks.name: Add GET connectivity-score route and register router in create_app()

tasks.description: Add an API-key auth dependency/middleware (src/connectivity/api/middleware/auth.py) that rejects unauthenticated or externally-originated requests with 401/403 before handler logic, gated by new Settings fields CONNECTIVITY_API_KEY_ENABLED and CONNECTIVITY_API_KEY (already referenced by tests/conftest.py). Document that the route sits behind the Connectivity API Gateway enforcing OAuth 2.0/OIDC (UC-C-004) with TLS 1.2+ and OWASP API Top 10 protections; the API key is sourced from GCP Secret Manager via Workload Identity, never committed.
tasks.name: Add internal API-key auth middleware and settings for internal-only access

tasks.description: Wrap the score computation in an in-process TTL cache keyed by (country, operator, brand, customer_id) with a configurable TTL (new setting CONNECTIVITY_SCORE_CACHE_TTL, default 60s) to raise cache-hit rate above the 80% architecture target and hold p95<500ms / p99<1000ms under load.
tasks.name: Add short-TTL (tenant, customer_id) score cache for the read-path SLO

tasks.description: Emit structlog single-line JSON audit logs per request (caller identity, customer_id scoped to the caller tenant, HTTP status, response latency) with no raw PII beyond the minimum identifier, and add OpenTelemetry FastAPI auto-instrumentation exporting to Cloud Trace. Connectivity-specific metrics stay BigQuery-based per the service's observability exception.
tasks.name: Add structured audit logging and OpenTelemetry tracing for the score endpoint

tasks.description: Add tests under services/connectivity/tests using the mock BigQuery adapter: unit tests for scoring formula, band boundaries, partial-metric handling, multi-device aggregation and data_freshness_days; integration tests for the route (200 with all three fields, 404 no-measurements, 401/403 unauthenticated, partial-metric); a cross-tenant isolation test asserting tenant A cannot receive tenant B data; and a load-test scenario at 2x expected peak asserting p95<500ms / p99<1000ms. Enforce the platform gate uv run pytest --cov --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=80.
tasks.name: Add unit, integration, cross-tenant, and load tests with 80% branch-coverage gate

test_strategy.coverage_notes: Run uv run pytest --cov --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=80 in services/connectivity as the required CI gate. New scoring, measurement-query, route, and auth code must clear the 80% branch-coverage gate.

gherkin_scenarios.then: the response is HTTP 404 and no data_freshness_days field is returned

gherkin_scenarios.given: a customer with measurements in the window but missing one of the three scored metrics
gherkin_scenarios.then: a score is still returned from the metrics present and 404 is not raised

gherkin_scenarios.given: computed sub-scores that place the weighted score exactly at a band boundary
gherkin_scenarios.then: the tie resolves to the lower band and the four bands are mutually exclusive across 0-100

gherkin_scenarios.then: it equals 5 (floor of full days elapsed), and equals 0 when the most recent measurement completed within the last 24 hours

gherkin_scenarios.given: a customer associated with multiple probes/CPE devices each with measurements in the window
gherkin_scenarios.then: all device measurements aggregate into exactly one customer-level score and status with no per-device breakdown

gherkin_scenarios.given: API-key enforcement enabled and a request lacking valid internal credentials
gherkin_scenarios.then: the request is rejected with HTTP 401/403 before any handler or query logic executes

gherkin_scenarios.given: measurements for the same customer_id existing under two different operator tenants
gherkin_scenarios.then: only tenant A measurements are queried and aggregated and tenant B rows are never returned
gherkin_scenarios.when: a caller authenticated for tenant A requests the score

gherkin_scenarios.then: the boundary validation returns a structured HTTP 400 without leaking internal identifiers or SQL errors and no query is executed

gherkin_scenarios.given: a score already computed for a (tenant, customer_id) within the cache TTL
gherkin_scenarios.then: it is served from the cache without re-querying BigQuery, keeping the response within the p95 budget
gherkin_scenarios.when: the same score request arrives again

gherkin_scenarios.given: any request to the score endpoint
gherkin_scenarios.then: a single-line JSON audit log is emitted with caller identity, customer_id, HTTP status and latency and contains no raw PII beyond the minimum identifier

Measure cache-hit rate under sustained load and assert it exceeds the 80% architecture target.

doc.title: Customer connectivity score endpoint

business_context.relevance: Answers spec question: How does the connectivity service currently authenticate and authorize internal-only endpoints intended for operations and support teams? Is there an existing role, scope, gateway, or permission mechanism these teams use?
business_context.summary: The connectivity service authenticates callers via API keys shared across all internal services; all services sit behind a common API gateway in production, and no separate role or scope mechanism specific to an internal operations/support tier exists beyond this shared scheme.

business_context.relevance: Answers spec question: What field or identifier represents a "customer" in the ingested SamKnows / speed-test measurement data, and can a single customer be associated with multiple probes or CPE devices whose measurements would need to be aggregated together?
business_context.summary: Customer identity is the canonical key for aggregating connectivity measurements; a single customer can be associated with multiple probes or CPE devices, so measurements from all associated devices must be aggregated to produce a customer-level view.

business_context.relevance: Answers spec question: Are there existing connectivity status/health band definitions (e.g. excellent / good / degraded / critical, or any RAG-style banding) used elsewhere in the connectivity service, dashboard, or CASAS architecture that a new score endpoint should align with?
business_context.summary: The existing Connectivity dashboard defines a three-state probe status band: Online (green), Degraded (orange), and Unknown/Offline (grey); the Consumer Experience Mapping layer uses a three-tier threshold indicator (green tick = good, amber = marginal, red cross = insufficient) per application category. No four-band excellent/good/degraded/critical scheme is defined anywhere in the KB.

business_context.relevance: Answers spec question: What read-path latency budget or SLO applies to connectivity service query/read API endpoints?
business_context.summary: The CASAS Connectivity Architect defines touchpoint APIs (C-App/C-Web/C-Care) at p95 < 500ms and p99 < 1000ms with 99.9% uptime and a cache hit rate target above 80%; no narrower SLO specific to internal read endpoints of the Connectivity Service is recorded.

compliance_constraints.applies_because: The endpoint returns per-customer data across OpCo markets; GDPR and local data-protection and data-residency regulations require that customer data is handled per-market and remains within its required jurisdiction (CON-009-005, CON-004-03, ADR-X002).

The CASAS multi-tenancy principle mandates country+operator+brand filtering on all customer data and prohibits exposing operator customer identifiers to third parties; the score is computed per customer and must enforce these tenant boundaries.

out_of_scope: Exposing the score on any consumer self-service surface (consumer app, web, or self-service portal); access is limited to internal operations and support tooling.
Automated remediation or any action triggered by a low score.
Alerting or notification when a customer's score degrades over time.
Returning a historical time-series or trend of the score; the endpoint reports only the current trailing-window value.
Changing how SamKnows measurements are ingested or which test types are collected.
Per-application consumer-experience mapping (e.g. streaming, gaming, video-call quality indicators).
outcomes: A GET request to /api/v1/customers/{customer_id}/connectivity-score for a customer that has at least one SamKnows test measurement in the trailing 30-day window returns a numeric score in the inclusive range 0-100 together with a status that is exactly one of: excellent, good, degraded, critical.
The score is a weighted average of three per-metric sub-scores with fixed weights: download speed contributes 50%, upload speed 25%, and latency 25%.

Each per-metric sub-score is expressed relative to the customer's provisioned plan rather than in raw units: throughput sub-scores reflect measured speed as a proportion of the customer's provisioned/plan speed (meeting or exceeding plan yields a maximal sub-score) and lower latency yields a higher sub-score, so two customers on different plan tiers who each fully meet their plan receive comparably high scores.

The status band is derived from the score with these boundaries (ties resolve to the lower band): score greater than 80 is excellent; greater than 60 and up to and including 80 is good; greater than 40 and up to and including 60 is degraded; 40 or below is critical. The bands are mutually exclusive and cover the whole 0-100 range.

When a customer is associated with multiple probes or CPE devices that have measurements in the window, all of their measurements are aggregated into a single customer-level score and status; the endpoint returns exactly one score per customer, never a per-device breakdown.
The measurement window is the 30 days immediately preceding the request (a rolling window), evaluated on each request by test completion time.
A GET for a customer_id that has no SamKnows measurements of any type in the trailing 30-day window returns HTTP 404; an absent-measurement customer is never reported as a zero score.

When measurements exist in the window but one or more of the three scored metrics has no measurement, a score is still returned from the metrics that are present; 404 is reserved strictly for the case where the customer has no measurements of any type in the window.

The endpoint is internal-only: it is accessible only to authenticated internal callers (operations and support teams) and is not exposed on any customer-facing channel; unauthenticated or externally-originated requests are rejected.
The endpoint meets the connectivity read-path service level: p95 response time under 500 ms and p99 under 1000 ms under expected operational load.

Per-customer data returned by the endpoint is handled in accordance with GDPR and per-market data-protection and data-residency rules: the response carries only the minimum customer data needed to express the score and status, and a customer's measurement data is processed within its required jurisdiction.

The score reflects only measurements belonging to the requested customer within their own country, operator, and brand tenant; data is filtered by country+operator+brand and never combined across tenants, and operator-internal customer identifiers are not exposed to any third party.

Every successful (HTTP 200) score response includes a data_freshness_days field alongside the score and status: a whole number giving the count of full days elapsed since the customer's most recent SamKnows test measurement of any type (download, upload, latency, jitter, or any other collected test), evaluated by test completion time and taken across all of the customer's associated probes and CPE devices; a measurement completed within the last 24 hours yields 0.

Because a score is only returned when the customer has at least one measurement in the trailing 30-day window, data_freshness_days is always within the inclusive range 0-30; it reflects the single most recent measurement across all of the customer's devices and is not present on the HTTP 404 no-measurements response.
body.problem: Operations and support teams have no at-a-glance measure of a customer's connectivity health. To judge whether a customer's line is healthy they must read and mentally aggregate raw individual SamKnows test measurements (download, upload, latency, jitter) across the recent past. During complaint triage or account review this is slow and inconsistent between operators. This work adds an internal-only read endpoint that summarizes a customer's last 30 days of already-ingested SamKnows measurements into a single 0-100 connectivity score and a coarse status band, so an operator gets a fast, consistent health read without manually inspecting raw measurements.
